app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1 — {{#unless automatic}}` is evaluated inside an `itemView="group-member"` item template whose context is the individual `member`, not the group controller, so `automatic` likely resolves against the wrong object, making the delete-link visibility logic unclear/fragile
app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit` param has no upper bound, allowing a client to request an arbitrarily large page of group members (minor DoS/resource use)
- — No other security issues found: admin group membership endpoints remain gated by AdminConstraint routes, and find_group still enforces guardian.ensure_can_see!

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` (which mutates the join table immediately) and then calls `group.save`, which does nothing for the removal and misleadingly implies the delete is not yet persisted

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `if group.save ... else ...`. For a HABTM/has_many :through association, `delete` on the association removes the join row immediately, so the subsequent `group.save` is redundant and its return value doesn’t reflect whether the member removal succeeded. This makes the code misleading and could cause incorrect error reporting if `group.save` were to fail for unrelated validation/state reasons, even though the deletion already happened.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1 — {{#unless automatic}}` is evaluated inside an `itemView="group-member"` item template whose context is the individual `member`, not the group controller, so `automatic` likely resolves against the wrong object, making the delete-link visibility logic unclear/fragile

adjudication.rationale: `group_member.hbs` uses `{{#unless automatic}}...{{/unless}}`, but the new `group-member` view (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/views/group-member.js.es6`) does not define/bind an `automatic` property. In `group.hbs` the members are rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, so inside the item view/template `automatic` is not clearly coming from the group/controller context. If it resolves to `undefined` in the item template context, `unless automatic` will evaluate truthy and show the remove link even for automatic groups (which the backend now rejects via `can_not_modify_automatic`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded UI behavior defect/fragility introduced by the new itemView template.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit` param has no upper bound, allowing a client to request an arbitrarily large page of group members (minor DoS/resource use)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit)` with no upper bound or clamping. This enables a client to request an arbitrarily large `limit`, potentially causing excessive DB/load (minor DoS). The change also expands pagination (and thus the unbounded `limit`) from only automatic groups previously to all groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - — No other security issues found: admin group membership endpoints remain gated by AdminConstraint routes, and find_group still enforces guardian.ensure_can_see!

adjudication.rationale: The finding asserts there are no additional security issues and cites correct protections shown in the diff (the new admin membership routes are inside the admin namespace with `constraints(AdminConstraint)` in `config/routes.rb`, and `GroupsController#find_group` still calls `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`). Since it does not identify a defect or actionable review issue in the changed code, it doesn’t qualify as a bug or important non-bug finding.
